articles.title: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.content:
Former Yahoo CEO and early Google engineer Marissa Mayer is catching a lot of flack for how she uses AI. Inan interviewabout her new app Dazzle, an AI assistant that learns from your camera roll, Mayer poses what she believes is an impressive flex for the product: It helped her come up with three bullet points about her 10-year-old daughter for a birthday presentation at school, describing her as “empathetic, creative, and an animal lover.”

It’s a vague description, like a generic horoscope — it could probably describe a lot of 10-year-olds.

Some onlookers, like progressive activist Leah Greenberg,marveledthat “the fact that Marissa Mayer would voluntarily disclose this to a reporter is a pretty good demonstration of how deeply the culture of Silicon Valley has diverged from the rest of humanity.”

"She thought it was perfect."www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/s…

Perhaps Mayer drew so much backlash because we have repeatedly observed sheltered billionaires suggest that we outsourcechild-rearing— one of life’s greatest tests of patience, humility, and kindness — to a computer that isincapable of understandinghuman emotion.

We’ve been primed for this frustration. Last year, OpenAI CEO Sam AltmantoldBored Ape ownerand late night host Jimmy Fallon on national television, “I cannot imagine … figuring out how to raise a newborn without ChatGPT.” The public didn’t love that comment, either, but Altman wasn’t phased by thenegativefeedback. A few months ago, he said on X that a “cool use case” of ChatGPT Work would be creating a podcast that talks about your kids’ upcoming birthdays or soccer games and “explain[s] your kids’ interests.” (He was brutallyratioedwithcommentslike, “What if you just talked to your children?”)

After publication, Mayer defended herself in a longX post. She claims she was not relying on Dazzle to explain her child to her, but rather, she was testing what her prototype could do — it resurfaced photos of “forgotten kindergarten projects,” like a “snake devenomer” or “sandcat playground,” illustrating her daughter’s creativity and care for animals.

Fair enough. But Mayerremarksin the same interview that people could also use her AI to outsource the mental load of “figuring out the theme for your child’s birthday party.” She says she’s used her app to plan a playdate for her daughter, book family activities on vacation, and decide what to be for Halloween. She even proposes that her AI assistant could coordinate plans with her husband’s AI assistant. When the reporter asks her if it’s depressing to imagine this “frictionless future… planned by AI,” Mayer replies, “I haven’t really thought that through.”

These leaders seem to write off the naysayers as part of a small, angry fringe group. Yet a Pew Research Centerstudyreports that 50% of U.S. adults think that AI will reduce people’s ability to form meaningful relationships. Only 5% of respondents said AI would make it easier to build these connections.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, however, joins his Silicon Valley kin in envisioning a world where our social needs are met via AI.

“The average American I think has, it’s fewer than three friends, three people they’d consider friends, and the average person has demand for meaningfully more, I think it’s like 15 friends,” Zuckerberg said last year on apodcast. “The average person wants more connectivity, connection than they have.”

Zuckerberg predicts that it will become more socially acceptable to outsource our emotional needs to AI therapists or even AI romantic partners. “There are all these things that are better about physical connections when you can have them,” he added. “But the reality is that people […] feel more alone a lot of the time than they would like.”

Zuckerberg goes on to explain how virtual reality embodiments of AI avatars are only growing more realistic. Meta seems to be more keen on improving our relationships with these approximations of humans, rather than between the actual billions of humans who use its platforms each day.

Maybe part of this stems from the culture of the tech industry, which prizes efficiency. People try to biohack their own bodies by optimizing theirsleep scheduleswith health trackers or injecting unregulated “peptide stacks” to maximize their productivity.

If you’re building electric vehicles or computer chips, then sure, efficiency is a clear North Star. But our relationships with other people are not a tech product that we’ve been challenged to ship with little capital as possible. Human relationships are inherently messy, but our connections with one another can be what gives our lives meaning. When we delegate those interactions to computers, we surrender the difficult, yet fulfilling experience of being people.

articles.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the ‘For You’ feed
articles.author: Aisha Malik
articles.content:
Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. The companyannouncedon Wednesday that users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”

The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across. The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined.

The company says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.

Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media, where algorithms play a significant role in shaping what users see.

With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.

Of course, not everyone will welcome the change, as some users may prefer the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined, rather than having recommended content mixed into their home feed. Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have alreadyexpressedtheirfrustrationwith the change.

Reddit says users can switch between feeds and return to the one they last viewed the next time they open the platform.

It’s worth noting that although Reddit has long recommended posts from outside users’ subscribed communities, the new layout gives those recommendations their own feed on the homepage.

“This new feed experience is a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant – an idea, a connection, a unique perspective, or even a new interest,” the company wrote in ablog post. “A more human internet is not just something you sit back and watch, it is something you find value in and want to participate in.”

The new feed experience is rolling out globally over the next few weeks, the company says.

articles.title: Amazon debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time smart clock, plus other upgraded devices
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.content:
Amazon unveiled fivenew Alexa devicestoday, including two new kinds of hardware: theAlexa Photo Frame, a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock.

The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s foray into the world of digital photo displays, a product category that has transcended from a clunky, last-minute holiday gift to a sleek, attractive way to look through your camera roll.

Aurais responsible for much of the growth in this category, so it’s no coincidence that the Alexa Photo Frame has a similar aesthetic feel: The screen is much easier on the eyes than the old, bright photo frames from years past. The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen.

Also like Aura, the Photo Frame’s 10-inch screen looks like a matte photograph, helping it blend in with other artwork on your wall.

Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts. Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos.

“It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring. It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release. You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them.

The Alexa Photo Frame ison sale now, and starts at $199.99 in Black, and $229 in Birch or Walnut wood.

Meanwhile, theEcho Timeclock seems to be a response to the growing sentiment that peopledon’t want to rely on their phonesfor alarms, setting morning reminders, or checking the weather.

“Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.”

Amazon says that theEcho Time, which costs $199.99, or $209.99 for aKidsversion, has opt-in sleep sensing tools. You can choose to set a smart alarm feature that wakes you up within a 10 to 60 minute window of your alarm time, and can wake you when it detects you’re in a lighter phase of sleep, so that it’s less jarring to begin your day.

Like the popularHatchalarm clocks, the clock can also mimic sunrise features to ease you awake.

Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices. We now get the Echo Show 16, a new Echo Dot, and Echo Studio with Home Camera.

The biggest upgrade to theEcho Dotis that it now includes a built-in smart home hub, which also includes aneero Wi-Fi extenderthat adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage, helping it connect to lights, locks, and thermostats around your home. The new Echo Dot is also powered by Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon chip, which is said to make it better at on-device processing to speed up conversations with its AI, Alexa+.

Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera. This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features.

“Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

The Echo Dot is available at $99.99, and the Echo Studio with Home Camera costs $249.99.

Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display. Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame. It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer. It can also function like a digital photo frame.

TheEcho Show 16is available for preorder for $499.99.

articles.title: VCs will make billions on Anthropic’s IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more
articles.author: Marina Temkin
articles.content:
Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms, including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital, are expected toreturn billions.

Yet, according toAnthropic’s S-1, none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly$14 billion positionis only about 1.5% of the company, according torecently reportedBloomberg figures.

While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO.

Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with a commitment to investup to $4 billionin the AI company. Since then, Amazon has poured billions more into Anthropic. Instead of taking stock up front, Amazon structured much of its investment as convertible notes, a type of debt that converts into shares upon an IPO or sale.

According to the S-1, Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30. That is Anthropic’s entire debt load. But as Anthropic’s valuation soared across successive funding rounds, the shares those notes will convert into became far more valuable. Amazon’s own filings valued its note holdings at$97.9 billionas of June 30.

As the value of Amazon’s convertible notes surged, Anthropic had to record the growing value of what it owes on its books. It reported the adjustments on its income statement under “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs,” a line that totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026. The charge is non-cash, meaning no money left the company.

Amazon’s notes could convert into as many as 1.84 billion shares, according to the S-1. But a cap limits Amazon to 12% of Anthropic’s “partially diluted” share count, a figure that counts some shares not yet issued, such as stock options. Amazon can waive the cap. Notes that can’t convert will stay outstanding and convert in later quarters, subject to the same limit.

But the notes are only part of Amazon’s holdings. It further invested $10 billion in nonvoting preferred stock (a type of equity) in the second quarter, according to Amazon’s quarterly report for the period ended June 30. Amazon did this by investing $5 billion in each of Anthropic’s last two funding rounds. Combined with the $8 billion it invested in the notes from 2023 through 2025, that brings Amazon’s total investment to about $18 billion.

Beyond its stock gains, Amazon will also continue to earn significant revenue from Anthropic, which has committed to spend at least $110 billion on AWS over the next 10 years.

Google, too, is set for a major windfall from both the listing and its cloud computing deals with Anthropic. The search giant held about 14% of Anthropic as of early last year, according tocourt filingsthat werereported by The New York Times, and has invested more since, including $10 billion in April. (Google was likely diluted in subsequent and massive funding rounds, with PitchBook analyst Harrison Rolfes telling TechCrunch he estimates its current stake at closer to 5.6%.) It has also secured at least $114 billion in cloud commitments from Anthropic through 2033.

While VCs set for massive paydays have little reason to complain, the S-1 makes it clear that the biggest winners of Anthropic’s IPO may well be tech giants like Amazon, which backed a would-be rival early on and now sells it much of the computing power it runs on.

The S-1 itself warns that some of those cloud providers also build rival AI models and that they may not always want the same things that Anthropic does.

articles.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
articles.author: Julie Bort
articles.content:
Nvidia on Wednesday releasedNemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open source speech dataset.

Nvidia boasts that Nemotron 3.5 can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks, including Hugging Face’sOpen ASR Leaderboard.

These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language. One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not livestreams.

Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chippowering new laptops, to Blackwell datacenter chips. It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yetpowerful Parakeet(1.1 billion parameters).

Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during a busy period of AI voice releases: Mistralshipped Voxtral 3earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce releasedLauna-Omni,its voice model.

articles.title: Kodiak lands first commercial deal to supply driverless trucks for public highways
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec
articles.content:
Kodiak AI will deliver 75 self-driving trucks to freight company DTL Transport starting in 2028. It’s the company’s first binding commercial deal for driverless big rigs that will run on public highways.

The contract, announced Wednesday, comes just ahead of Kodiak’s next big milestone: pulling human safety operators out of the cab to begin operating a driverless highway service in December. The company, whichwent publicin September 2025, plans to launch that service by carrying goods for Ikea on Interstate 45 between Dallas and Houston.

DTL Transport, a California midmarket trucking company that hauls fresh produce and goods to grocery chains, plans to use the self-driving trucks on multiple interstate highway routes, starting with Dallas to El Paso, Texas, and Interstate 20 between Dallas and Atlanta. Kodiak has already conducted testing and operations on those two routes.

“One of the things that we love about midmarket carriers (like DTL) is that they are able to move with fast execution speed, much more at the speed of a startup or a small company or a tech company like Kodiak, and that they just want to get stuff done,” Kodiak founder and CEO Don Burnette told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview. “It’s easier for them to integrate into their fleet because they’re not as large, and we think that this is a real turning point for the self-driving industry in general.”

The contract should give Kodiak a revenue boost and a positive benchmark. Its shares have fallen 87% from their opening-day price. It also puts Kodiak on a path to become an “asset-light” technology supplier, meaning it would sell its technology rather than own and run trucks itself — agoal it shareswith competitor Aurora Innovation.

Today, Kodiak has a number of customers under a trucking-as-a-service (TaaS) model, including Charger USA, Roehl Transport, and Werner Enterprises. Under this business model, Kodiak owns and operates the self-driving trucks as a third-party carrier on behalf of other companies. It currently carries freight for these companies on a few routes in Texas. Kodiak generates revenue carrying freight daily for these companies on three active routes, but Burnette described these operations as still being in pilot stage.

Ultimately, Kodiak wants to move to a driver-as-a-service (DaaS) model, in which customers own and operate the trucks. Kodiak licenses its technology, charging customers by the mile for the duration of the contract. DTL is Kodiak’s first on-highway DaaS customer, a relationship that was forged during a pilot program last month in California. In that pilot, Kodiak autonomously hauled perishable goods for DTL about 225 miles along Interstate 5 and California State Route 99 between Fresno, California, and Los Angeles, with a human safety operator behind the wheel.

“You have to prove out the technology first using your own truck, show them that it works, show them that it’s safe, show them that it integrates,” Burnette said, describing the TaaS model. “And then we want to be asset light. We don’t want to be in the business of running a trucking company.”

Atlas Energy Solutions has been a DaaS customer since 2024. Technically, Atlas was Kodiak’s first customer under a binding commercial contract, but its driverless trucks operate in off-road settings in West Texas’ remote Permian Basin. Atlas currently owns and operates 35 driverless trucks equipped with Kodiak’s self-driving system. Burnette said Kodiak is on track to have as many as 100 in service there by mid-2027.

Kodiak didn’t reveal the value of the deal with DTL Transport. However, its public2025 investor presentationoffers some clues about the contract’s potential value.

In that document, Kodiak forecast annual recurring revenue of $150,000 to $190,000 per truck. That forecast rests on several assumptions, including a per-mile licensing fee of about $0.97 (in line with current human driver costs per mile), annual mileage of about 225,000 miles a year per truck, and other factors.

Assuming those projections bear out, the deal with DTL Transport could generate at least about $11.2 million in annual recurring revenue once all 75 trucks are delivered.

articles.title: South Korea’s financial industry hit by fresh wave of cyberattacks
articles.author: Kate Park
articles.content:
South Korea’s financial institutions have been hit by another wave of cyberattacks, highlighting the growing risk of AI-driven hacking in Asia. The latest incidents affect brokerages Daishin Securities and Mirae Asset Global Investments, as well as the crypto exchange Bithumb.

The incident comes roughly a month after aseries of cyberattackstargeting South Korean financial institutions, raising concerns about vulnerabilities beyond just the country’s banking systems. Security researcherslinkedthe September wave of attacks on South Korea to a suspected China-based hacker who relied on an AI penetration testing tool called Artex, though officials are still investigating the root cause of the latest breaches.

According to local news,Daishin reported a cyberattack that exposed the personal information of 38,490 customers, including names, email addresses, and mobile phone numbers. The company has notified affected customers, is cooperating with authorities in the investigation, and will compensate for any losses as required by law.

Meanwhile, Mirae and Bithumb reported separate cybersecurity incidents on Wednesday, perlocal media, though neither has confirmed that customer data was taken.

South Korea’s financial regulator has called for stronger cybersecurity measures following a string of attacks on financial firms and government agencies,per officialsin Seoul on Wednesday. The country also plans to conduct security checks on dozens of IT systems in the private sector.

Yesterday,Japan reporteda cybersecurity incident involving GMO Internet, following a series of attacks on its financial institutions. The wave of cyberattacks across Asia underscore growing cybersecurity challenges in the region, often as a result of years of weak cybersecurity; though, investigators have not established a connection between the incidents.

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC), Daishin Securities, Bithumb, and Mirae Asset Global Investments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.content:
After years of resisting, Apple todaylauncheda MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with itsTouch Bar on a MacBook Pro, which it laterwent on to remove.

The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.

To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound.

The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors.

Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant.

The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399.

Consumers can place the pre-order for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6.

The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Turnus, who also introducedthe company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September. Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea  “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumours of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearlythree years before today’s introduction.

The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with theM6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999.

articles.title: Xreal Aura is a new wired headset powered by Android XR
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.content:
At the Android Developer Summit on Wednesday, Google’ssmart glasses partnerXreallaunched its new Xreal Aura wired smart glasses, powered by the Android XR and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite platforms. The companieshad teased the glasses earlier in the yearat Google’s I/O developer conference.

As Meta expands its push into smart glasses, competitors like Apple and Google are keen to release their own devices. Much like it did with Android smartphones, Google is relying on an assortment of partners, including Samsung and Xreal, to bring devices powered by its Android XR platform to consumers.

The new Xreal Aura smart glasses are tethered to a smartphone-like device for processing power, rather than handling all the computing themselves. The glasses then display the content in the wearer’s field of view.

The device’s design, meanwhile, is closer to Meta’s smart glasses than Apple’s Vision Pro, which is a larger headset.

Xreal Aura uses Sony’s Micro-OLED display with 1200p resolution at 120Hz and a 95-degree field of view — screen specs that put the glasses above the Ray-Ban Meta Display on paper. However, Xreal’s smart glasses are heavier at 95 grams compared to Meta’s 69 grams, and you have to carry the puck.

At launch, the Aura supports many popular Google Play apps and games along with specific XR experiences, including NBA App for Android XR, Nevatars, Fallout: Factions, Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars, NASCAR XR App, and San Francisco Ballet Company’s The Nutcracker.

Users can opt to plug a computer or handheld gaming console directly into the Xreal Aura via USB-C to make it an augmented display. The device can also allow for various entertainment and productivity use cases by spinning up a multi-monitor setup or a big virtual screen.

For audio, the Xreal Aura uses Bose’s tech to power its sound while watching videos or listening to music.

Given that the new smart glasses are powered by Android XR, Gemini is available to users as a Q&A assistant and can help users to understand on-screen context.

The Xreal Aura is available to order starting today in the United States, Canada, Japan, andSouth Korea. The 12GB + 256GB version costs $1,279 with a limited launch price of $1,099 through December, and the 16GB + 512GB version is priced at $1,499 with a launch price of $1,299 through December. The company said it will start shipping by Mid-November.

In May, Xreal CEO Chi Xu told TechCrunch that buildinga smart glass business is hard and everyone is losing money. He also said that the Aura glasses will have a wide range of use cases, and the industry has reached an inflection point of having the right hardware, software, and design smart glasses to reach scale.

“You need all the key pieces ready — you need the hardware ready, the operating system needs to be ready, and then you need a great user interface,” Xu said at that time.
